title: Keralam government to hold talks with LPST protesters

ai.summary: The Kerala government plans talks with LPST Rankholders' Association after 133 days of protest over delayed teacher appointments and recruitment system changes.

facts.claim: The Keralam government will hold talks with the representatives of the All Kerala Lower Primary School Teachers (LPST) Rankholders’ Association who have been on an agitation in front of the Secretariat for the past 133 days.
facts.quote: The Keralam government will hold talks with the representatives of the All Kerala Lower Primary School Teachers (LPST) Rankholders’ Association who have been on an agitation in front of the Secretariat for the past 133 days.

facts.claim: The Chief Minister’s Office on Sunday informed the protesters that the government is willing for talks.
facts.quote: The Chief Minister’s Office on Sunday informed the protesters that the government is willing for talks.

facts.claim: S. Valarmathi, the association secretary, who is on a fast-unto-death protest, said the agitation will be withdrawn only if the government agrees to the demands.
facts.quote: S. Valarmathi, the association secretary, who is on a fast-unto-death protest, said the agitation will be withdrawn only if the government agrees to the demands.

facts.claim: The LPST rank-holders began their protest over the delay in appointing candidates from the Kerala Public Service Commission (PSC) rank list to lower primary school teacher (LPST) posts, along with demands for changes to the teacher-recruitment system and teacher-student ratio.
facts.quote: The LPST rank-holders began their protest over the delay in appointing candidates from the Kerala Public Service Commission (PSC) rank list to lower primary school teacher (LPST) posts, along with demands for changes to the teacher-recruitment system and teacher-student ratio.

facts.claim: The agitation, which began as a demand for appointment orders, has now expanded into a broader dispute over how teaching vacancies are calculated, reported and filled.
facts.quote: The agitation, which began as a demand for appointment orders, has now expanded into a broader dispute over how teaching vacancies are calculated, reported and filled.

facts.claim: The LPST rank list came into effect in all 14 districts on May 31, 2025. The list reportedly has around 11,758 candidates, but fewer than 500 appointments had been made by August, according to reports.
facts.quote: The LPST rank list came into effect in all 14 districts on May 31, 2025. The list reportedly has around 11,758 candidates, but fewer than 500 appointments had been made by August, according to reports.

ai.background_note: The LPST Rankholders’ Association has been protesting for 133 days over delayed appointments from the Kerala PSC rank list, which was implemented in May 2025 with 11,758 candidates but fewer than 500 appointments by August.
